title: 13.3 A Cryo-BiCMOS Controller for 9Be+-Trapped-Ion-Based Quantum Computers
problem: Trapped-ion quantum computers require cryogenic control electronics operating at ~4K to interface with ion traps; existing digital controllers consume excessive power and limit qubit scalability.
motivation: 9Be+ trapped ions offer long coherence times (T2 up to hours), high single-qubit fidelity (10^-6), and two-qubit gate fidelities near fault-tolerance threshold (10^-4); QCCD architecture enables scalable all-to-all connectivity but needs cryogenic control to maintain qubit coherence.
method: The controller operates at 4K by combining bipolar transistors—which maintain good electrical performance at cryogenic temperatures—with CMOS technology for miniaturization and integration. It uses QCCD (quantum-charge-coupled-device) control to manage two key operations: shuttling trapped ions between different trap regions and entangling qubits for quantum computation.
key_novelty: Integrating bipolar and CMOS circuits that work at cryogenic temperatures with QCCD control architecture unlocks the ability to scale up trapped-ion quantum computers.
contributions: Cryo-BiCMOS controller design for 4K operation in ion trap systems
Supports QCCD architecture for scalable qubit connectivity
Maintains high qubit fidelity while reducing system power and complexity
Enables ion shuttling and two-qubit entanglement control
baselines: Room-temperature control electronics (high latency, coherence loss)
Previous cryo designs without full QCCD support
limitations: Abstract provides qubit specifications but does not detail controller power consumption, operating voltage range, or scalability limits for N qubits.
primary_theme: Cryo-BiCMOS control for scalable trapped-ion quantum computers
